properties.name: reasoning_effort
properties.description:
**o-series models only** 

Constrains effort on reasoning for 
[reasoning models](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/reasoning).
Currently supported values are `low`, `medium`, and `high`. Reducing
reasoning effort can result in faster responses and fewer tokens used
on reasoning in a response.

properties.name: max_completion_tokens
properties.description: An upper bound for the number of tokens that can be generated for a completion, including visible output tokens and [reasoning tokens](/docs/guides/reasoning).

properties.name: frequency_penalty
properties.description:
Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on
their existing frequency in the text so far, decreasing the model's
likelihood to repeat the same line verbatim.

properties.name: presence_penalty
properties.description:
Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on
whether they appear in the text so far, increasing the model's likelihood
to talk about new topics.

properties.name: web_search_options
properties.description:
This tool searches the web for relevant results to use in a response.
Learn more about the [web search tool](/docs/guides/tools-web-search?api-mode=chat).

properties.name: user_location
properties.description: Approximate location parameters for the search.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of location approximation. Always `approximate`.

properties.name: approximate
properties.description: Approximate location parameters for the search.

properties.name: country
properties.description:
The two-letter 
[ISO country code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1) of the user,
e.g. `US`.

properties.name: region
properties.description: Free text input for the region of the user, e.g. `California`.

properties.name: city
properties.description: Free text input for the city of the user, e.g. `San Francisco`.

properties.name: timezone
properties.description:
The [IANA timezone](https://timeapi.io/documentation/iana-timezones) 
of the user, e.g. `America/Los_Angeles`.

properties.name: search_context_size
properties.description:
High level guidance for the amount of context window space to use for the 
search. One of `low`, `medium`, or `high`. `medium` is the default.

properties.name: top_logprobs
properties.description:
An integer between 0 and 20 specifying the number of most likely tokens to
return at each token position, each with an associated log probability.
`logprobs` must be set to `true` if this parameter is used.

properties.name: response_format
properties.description:
An object specifying the format that the model must output.

Setting to `{ "type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {...} }` enables
Structured Outputs which ensures the model will match your supplied JSON
schema. Learn more in the [Structured Outputs
guide](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

Setting to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables the older JSON mode, which
ensures the message the model generates is valid JSON. Using `json_schema`
is preferred for models that support it.

properties.name: Text
properties.description: Default response format. Used to generate text responses.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of response format being defined. Always `text`.

properties.name: JSON schema
properties.description:
JSON Schema response format. Used to generate structured JSON responses.
Learn more about [Structured Outputs](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of response format being defined. Always `json_schema`.

properties.name: json_schema
properties.description: Structured Outputs configuration options, including a JSON Schema.

properties.name: description
properties.description:
A description of what the response format is for, used by the model to
determine how to respond in the format.

properties.name: name
properties.description:
The name of the response format. Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain
underscores and dashes, with a maximum length of 64.

properties.name: schema
properties.description:
The schema for the response format, described as a JSON Schema object.
Learn how to build JSON schemas [here](https://json-schema.org/).

properties.name: strict
properties.description:
Whether to enable strict schema adherence when generating the output.
If set to true, the model will always follow the exact schema defined
in the `schema` field. Only a subset of JSON Schema is supported when
`strict` is `true`. To learn more, read the [Structured Outputs
guide](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

properties.name: JSON object
properties.description:
JSON object response format. An older method of generating JSON responses.
Using `json_schema` is recommended for models that support it. Note that the
model will not generate JSON without a system or user message instructing it
to do so.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of response format being defined. Always `json_object`.

properties.name: audio
properties.description:
Parameters for audio output. Required when audio output is requested with
`modalities: ["audio"]`. [Learn more](/docs/guides/audio).

properties.name: format
properties.description:
Specifies the output audio format. Must be one of `wav`, `mp3`, `flac`,
`opus`, or `pcm16`.

properties.name: store
properties.description:
Whether or not to store the output of this chat completion request for 
use in our [model distillation](/docs/guides/distillation) or
[evals](/docs/guides/evals) products.

properties.name: stream
properties.description:
If set to true, the model response data will be streamed to the client
as it is generated using [server-sent events](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Server-sent_events/Using_server-sent_events#Event_stream_format).
See the [Streaming section below](/docs/api-reference/chat/streaming)
for more information, along with the [streaming responses](/docs/guides/streaming-responses)
guide for more information on how to handle the streaming events.

properties.name: stop
properties.description:
Not supported with latest reasoning models `o3` and `o4-mini`.

Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating further tokens. The
returned text will not contain the stop sequence.

properties.name: logit_bias
properties.description:
Modify the likelihood of specified tokens appearing in the completion.

Accepts a JSON object that maps tokens (specified by their token ID in the
tokenizer) to an associated bias value from -100 to 100. Mathematically,
the bias is added to the logits generated by the model prior to sampling.
The exact effect will vary per model, but values between -1 and 1 should
decrease or increase likelihood of selection; values like -100 or 100
should result in a ban or exclusive selection of the relevant token.

properties.name: logprobs
properties.description:
Whether to return log probabilities of the output tokens or not. If true,
returns the log probabilities of each output token returned in the
`content` of `message`.

properties.name: max_tokens
properties.description:
The maximum number of [tokens](/tokenizer) that can be generated in the
chat completion. This value can be used to control
[costs](https://openai.com/api/pricing/) for text generated via API.

This value is now deprecated in favor of `max_completion_tokens`, and is
not compatible with [o-series models](/docs/guides/reasoning).

properties.name: n
properties.description: How many chat completion choices to generate for each input message. Note that you will be charged based on the number of generated tokens across all of the choices. Keep `n` as `1` to minimize costs.

properties.name: prediction
properties.description:
Configuration for a [Predicted Output](/docs/guides/predicted-outputs),
which can greatly improve response times when large parts of the model
response are known ahead of time. This is most common when you are
regenerating a file with only minor changes to most of the content.

properties.name: Static Content
properties.description:
Static predicted output content, such as the content of a text file that is
being regenerated.

properties.name: type
properties.description:
The type of the predicted content you want to provide. This type is
currently always `content`.

properties.name: Text content
properties.description:
The content used for a Predicted Output. This is often the
text of a file you are regenerating with minor changes.

properties.name: Array of content parts
properties.description: An array of content parts with a defined type. Supported options differ based on the [model](/docs/models) being used to generate the response. Can contain text inputs.

properties.name: items
properties.description: Learn about [text inputs](/docs/guides/text-generation).

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of the content part.

properties.name: text
properties.description: The text content.

properties.name: seed
properties.description:
This feature is in Beta.
If specified, our system will make a best effort to sample deterministically, such that repeated requests with the same `seed` and parameters should return the same result.
Determinism is not guaranteed, and you should refer to the `system_fingerprint` response parameter to monitor changes in the backend.

properties.name: stream_options
properties.description: Options for streaming response. Only set this when you set `stream: true`.

properties.name: include_usage
properties.description:
If set, an additional chunk will be streamed before the `data: [DONE]`
message. The `usage` field on this chunk shows the token usage statistics
for the entire request, and the `choices` field will always be an empty
array. 

All other chunks will also include a `usage` field, but with a null
value. **NOTE:** If the stream is interrupted, you may not receive the
final usage chunk which contains the total token usage for the request.

properties.name: tools
properties.description: A list of tools the model may call. Currently, only functions are supported as a tool. Use this to provide a list of functions the model may generate JSON inputs for. A max of 128 functions are supported.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of the tool. Currently, only `function` is supported.

properties.name: description
properties.description: A description of what the function does, used by the model to choose when and how to call the function.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name of the function to be called. Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain underscores and dashes, with a maximum length of 64.

properties.name: parameters
properties.description:
The parameters the functions accepts, described as a JSON Schema object. See the [guide](/docs/guides/function-calling) for examples, and the [JSON Schema reference](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/) for documentation about the format. 

Omitting `parameters` defines a function with an empty parameter list.

properties.name: strict
properties.description: Whether to enable strict schema adherence when generating the function call. If set to true, the model will follow the exact schema defined in the `parameters` field. Only a subset of JSON Schema is supported when `strict` is `true`. Learn more about Structured Outputs in the [function calling guide](docs/guides/function-calling).

properties.name: tool_choice
properties.description:
Controls which (if any) tool is called by the model.
`none` means the model will not call any tool and instead generates a message.
`auto` means the model can pick between generating a message or calling one or more tools.
`required` means the model must call one or more tools.
Specifying a particular tool via `{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "my_function"}}` forces the model to call that tool.

`none` is the default when no tools are present. `auto` is the default if tools are present.

properties.name: tool_choice
properties.description: `none` means the model will not call any tool and instead generates a message. `auto` means the model can pick between generating a message or calling one or more tools. `required` means the model must call one or more tools.

properties.name: tool_choice
properties.description: Specifies a tool the model should use. Use to force the model to call a specific function.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of the tool. Currently, only `function` is supported.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name of the function to call.

properties.name: parallel_tool_calls
properties.description: Whether to enable [parallel function calling](/docs/guides/function-calling#configuring-parallel-function-calling) during tool use.

properties.name: function_call
properties.description:
Deprecated in favor of `tool_choice`.

Controls which (if any) function is called by the model.

`none` means the model will not call a function and instead generates a
message.

`auto` means the model can pick between generating a message or calling a
function.

Specifying a particular function via `{"name": "my_function"}` forces the
model to call that function.

`none` is the default when no functions are present. `auto` is the default
if functions are present.

properties.name: function_call
properties.description: `none` means the model will not call a function and instead generates a message. `auto` means the model can pick between generating a message or calling a function.

properties.name: function_call
properties.description: Specifying a particular function via `{"name": "my_function"}` forces the model to call that function.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name of the function to call.

properties.name: functions
properties.description:
Deprecated in favor of `tools`.

properties.description: A description of what the function does, used by the model to choose when and how to call the function.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name of the function to be called. Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain underscores and dashes, with a maximum length of 64.

properties.name: parameters
properties.description:

Omitting `parameters` defines a function with an empty parameter list.

properties.name: service_tier
properties.description:
Specifies the latency tier to use for processing the request. This parameter is relevant for customers subscribed to the scale tier service:
  - If set to 'auto', and the Project is Scale tier enabled, the system
    will utilize scale tier credits until they are exhausted.
  - If set to 'auto', and the Project is not Scale tier enabled, the request will be processed using the default service tier with a lower uptime SLA and no latency guarentee.

  - If set to 'flex', the request will be processed with the Flex Processing service tier. [Learn more](/docs/guides/flex-processing).

properties.name: model
properties.description: ID of the model to use. You can use the [List models](/docs/api-reference/models/list) API to see all of your available models, or see our [Model overview](/docs/models) for descriptions of them.

properties.name: prompt
properties.description:
The prompt(s) to generate completions for, encoded as a string, array of strings, array of tokens, or array of token arrays.

Note that <|endoftext|> is the document separator that the model sees during training, so if a prompt is not specified the model will generate as if from the beginning of a new document.

properties.name: best_of
properties.description:
Generates `best_of` completions server-side and returns the "best" (the one with the highest log probability per token). Results cannot be streamed.

When used with `n`, `best_of` controls the number of candidate completions and `n` specifies how many to return – `best_of` must be greater than `n`.

**Note:** Because this parameter generates many completions, it can quickly consume your token quota. Use carefully and ensure that you have reasonable settings for `max_tokens` and `stop`.

properties.name: echo
properties.description: Echo back the prompt in addition to the completion

properties.name: frequency_penalty
properties.description:
Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on their existing frequency in the text so far, decreasing the model's likelihood to repeat the same line verbatim.

[See more information about frequency and presence penalties.](/docs/guides/text-generation)

properties.name: logit_bias
properties.description:
Modify the likelihood of specified tokens appearing in the completion.

Accepts a JSON object that maps tokens (specified by their token ID in the GPT tokenizer) to an associated bias value from -100 to 100. You can use this [tokenizer tool](/tokenizer?view=bpe) to convert text to token IDs. Mathematically, the bias is added to the logits generated by the model prior to sampling. The exact effect will vary per model, but values between -1 and 1 should decrease or increase likelihood of selection; values like -100 or 100 should result in a ban or exclusive selection of the relevant token.

As an example, you can pass `{"50256": -100}` to prevent the <|endoftext|> token from being generated.

properties.name: logprobs
properties.description:
Include the log probabilities on the `logprobs` most likely output tokens, as well the chosen tokens. For example, if `logprobs` is 5, the API will return a list of the 5 most likely tokens. The API will always return the `logprob` of the sampled token, so there may be up to `logprobs+1` elements in the response.

The maximum value for `logprobs` is 5.

properties.name: max_tokens
properties.description:
The maximum number of [tokens](/tokenizer) that can be generated in the completion.

The token count of your prompt plus `max_tokens` cannot exceed the model's context length. [Example Python code](https://cookbook.openai.com/examples/how_to_count_tokens_with_tiktoken) for counting tokens.

properties.name: n
properties.description:
How many completions to generate for each prompt.

**Note:** Because this parameter generates many completions, it can quickly consume your token quota. Use carefully and ensure that you have reasonable settings for `max_tokens` and `stop`.

properties.name: presence_penalty
properties.description:
Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on whether they appear in the text so far, increasing the model's likelihood to talk about new topics.

[See more information about frequency and presence penalties.](/docs/guides/text-generation)

properties.name: seed
properties.description:
If specified, our system will make a best effort to sample deterministically, such that repeated requests with the same `seed` and parameters should return the same result.

Determinism is not guaranteed, and you should refer to the `system_fingerprint` response parameter to monitor changes in the backend.

properties.name: stop
properties.description:
Not supported with latest reasoning models `o3` and `o4-mini`.

Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating further tokens. The
returned text will not contain the stop sequence.

properties.name: stream
properties.description: Whether to stream back partial progress. If set, tokens will be sent as data-only [server-sent events](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Server-sent_events/Using_server-sent_events#Event_stream_format) as they become available, with the stream terminated by a `data: [DONE]` message. [Example Python code](https://cookbook.openai.com/examples/how_to_stream_completions).

properties.name: stream_options
properties.description: Options for streaming response. Only set this when you set `stream: true`.

properties.name: include_usage
properties.description:
If set, an additional chunk will be streamed before the `data: [DONE]`
message. The `usage` field on this chunk shows the token usage statistics
for the entire request, and the `choices` field will always be an empty
array. 

All other chunks will also include a `usage` field, but with a null
value. **NOTE:** If the stream is interrupted, you may not receive the
final usage chunk which contains the total token usage for the request.

properties.name: suffix
properties.description:
The suffix that comes after a completion of inserted text.

This parameter is only supported for `gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct`.

properties.name: temperature
properties.description:
What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.

We generally recommend altering this or `top_p` but not both.

properties.name: top_p
properties.description:
An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.

We generally recommend altering this or `temperature` but not both.

properties.name: user
properties.description: A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to monitor and detect abuse. [Learn more](/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#end-user-ids).

Your dataset must be formatted as a JSONL file. Additionally, you must upload your file with the purpose `fine-tune`.

properties.name: suffix

properties.name: validation_file

If you provide this file, the data is used to generate validation
metrics periodically during fine-tuning. These metrics can be viewed in
the fine-tuning results file.
The same data should not be present in both train and validation files.

Your dataset must be formatted as a JSONL file. You must upload your file with the purpose `fine-tune`.

See the [fine-tuning guide](/docs/guides/fine-tuning) for more details.

properties.name: entity

If a seed is not specified, one will be generated for you.

properties.name: image
properties.description:
The image(s) to edit. Must be a supported image file or an array of images.

For `gpt-image-1`, each image should be a `png`, `webp`, or `jpg` file less 
than 25MB. You can provide up to 16 images.

For `dall-e-2`, you can only provide one image, and it should be a square 
`png` file less than 4MB.

properties.name: prompt
properties.description: A text description of the desired image(s). The maximum length is 1000 characters for `dall-e-2`, and 32000 characters for `gpt-image-1`.

properties.name: mask
properties.description: An additional image whose fully transparent areas (e.g. where alpha is zero) indicate where `image` should be edited. If there are multiple images provided, the mask will be applied on the first image. Must be a valid PNG file, less than 4MB, and have the same dimensions as `image`.

properties.name: model
properties.description: The model to use for image generation. Only `dall-e-2` and `gpt-image-1` are supported. Defaults to `dall-e-2` unless a parameter specific to `gpt-image-1` is used.

properties.name: n
properties.description: The number of images to generate. Must be between 1 and 10.

properties.name: size
properties.description: The size of the generated images. Must be one of `1024x1024`, `1536x1024` (landscape), `1024x1536` (portrait), or `auto` (default value) for `gpt-image-1`, and one of `256x256`, `512x512`, or `1024x1024` for `dall-e-2`.

properties.name: response_format
properties.description: The format in which the generated images are returned. Must be one of `url` or `b64_json`. URLs are only valid for 60 minutes after the image has been generated. This parameter is only supported for `dall-e-2`, as `gpt-image-1` will always return base64-encoded images.

properties.name: user
properties.description: A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to monitor and detect abuse. [Learn more](/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#end-user-ids).

properties.name: quality
properties.description: The quality of the image that will be generated. `high`, `medium` and `low` are only supported for `gpt-image-1`. `dall-e-2` only supports `standard` quality. Defaults to `auto`.

properties.name: prompt
properties.description: A text description of the desired image(s). The maximum length is 32000 characters for `gpt-image-1`, 1000 characters for `dall-e-2` and 4000 characters for `dall-e-3`.

properties.name: model
properties.description: The model to use for image generation. One of `dall-e-2`, `dall-e-3`, or `gpt-image-1`. Defaults to `dall-e-2` unless a parameter specific to `gpt-image-1` is used.

properties.name: n
properties.description: The number of images to generate. Must be between 1 and 10. For `dall-e-3`, only `n=1` is supported.

properties.name: quality
properties.description:
The quality of the image that will be generated. 

- `auto` (default value) will automatically select the best quality for the given model.
- `high`, `medium` and `low` are supported for `gpt-image-1`.
- `hd` and `standard` are supported for `dall-e-3`.
- `standard` is the only option for `dall-e-2`.

properties.name: response_format
properties.description: The format in which generated images with `dall-e-2` and `dall-e-3` are returned. Must be one of `url` or `b64_json`. URLs are only valid for 60 minutes after the image has been generated. This parameter isn't supported for `gpt-image-1` which will always return base64-encoded images.

properties.name: output_format
properties.description: The format in which the generated images are returned. This parameter is only supported for `gpt-image-1`. Must be one of `png`, `jpeg`, or `webp`.

properties.name: output_compression
properties.description: The compression level (0-100%) for the generated images. This parameter is only supported for `gpt-image-1` with the `webp` or `jpeg` output formats, and defaults to 100.

properties.name: size
properties.description: The size of the generated images. Must be one of `1024x1024`, `1536x1024` (landscape), `1024x1536` (portrait), or `auto` (default value) for `gpt-image-1`, one of `256x256`, `512x512`, or `1024x1024` for `dall-e-2`, and one of `1024x1024`, `1792x1024`, or `1024x1792` for `dall-e-3`.

properties.name: moderation
properties.description: Control the content-moderation level for images generated by `gpt-image-1`. Must be either `low` for less restrictive filtering or `auto` (default value).

properties.name: background
properties.description:
Allows to set transparency for the background of the generated image(s). 
This parameter is only supported for `gpt-image-1`. Must be one of 
`transparent`, `opaque` or `auto` (default value). When `auto` is used, the 
model will automatically determine the best background for the image.

If `transparent`, the output format needs to support transparency, so it 
should be set to either `png` (default value) or `webp`.

properties.name: style
properties.description: The style of the generated images. This parameter is only supported for `dall-e-3`. Must be one of `vivid` or `natural`. properties.name: temperature
properties.description: What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.

properties.name: top_p
properties.description:
An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.

We generally recommend altering this or temperature but not both.

properties.description: The maximum number of prompt tokens that may be used over the course of the run. The run will make a best effort to use only the number of prompt tokens specified, across multiple turns of the run. If the run exceeds the number of prompt tokens specified, the run will end with status `incomplete`. See `incomplete_details` for more info.

properties.name: max_completion_tokens
properties.description: The maximum number of completion tokens that may be used over the course of the run. properties.name: response_format
properties.description:
Specifies the format that the model must output. Compatible with [GPT-4o](/docs/models#gpt-4o), [GPT-4 Turbo](/docs/models#gpt-4-turbo-and-gpt-4), and all GPT-3.5 Turbo models since `gpt-3.5-turbo-1106`.

Setting to `{ "type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {...} }` enables Structured Outputs which ensures the model will match your supplied JSON schema. Learn more in the [Structured Outputs guide](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

Setting to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables JSON mode, which ensures the message the model generates is valid JSON.

**Important:** when using JSON mode, you **must** also instruct the model to produce JSON yourself via a system or user message. Without this, the model may generate an unending stream of whitespace until the generation reaches the token limit, resulting in a long-running and seemingly "stuck" request. Also note that the message content may be partially cut off if `finish_reason="length"`, which indicates the generation exceeded `max_tokens` or the conversation exceeded the max context length.

The run will make a best effort to use only the number of prompt tokens specified, across multiple turns of the run. If the run exceeds the number of prompt tokens specified, the run will end with status `incomplete`. See `incomplete_details` for more info.

properties.name: max_completion_tokens
properties.description: The maximum number of completion tokens that may be used over the course of the run. The run will make a best effort to use only the number of completion tokens specified, across multiple turns of the run. If the run exceeds the number of completion tokens specified, the run will end with status `incomplete`. See `incomplete_details` for more info.

properties.name: parallel_tool_calls
properties.description: Whether to enable [parallel function calling](/docs/guides/function-calling#configuring-parallel-function-calling) during tool use.

properties.name: response_format
properties.description:
Specifies the format that the model must output. Compatible with [GPT-4o](/docs/models#gpt-4o), [GPT-4 Turbo](/docs/models#gpt-4-turbo-and-gpt-4), and all GPT-3.5 Turbo models since `gpt-3.5-turbo-1106`.

Setting to `{ "type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {...} }` enables Structured Outputs which ensures the model will match your supplied JSON schema. Learn more in the [Structured Outputs guide](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

Setting to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables JSON mode, which ensures the message the model generates is valid JSON.

**Important:** when using JSON mode, you **must** also instruct the model to produce JSON yourself via a system or user message. Without this, the model may generate an unending stream of whitespace until the generation reaches the token limit, resulting in a long-running and seemingly "stuck" request. Also note that the message content may be partially cut off if `finish_reason="length"`, which indicates the generation exceeded `max_tokens` or the conversation exceeded the max context length.

If set to true, the model will always follow the exact schema defined

guide](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

properties.name: temperature
properties.description: The sampling temperature, between 0 and 1. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. If set to 0, the model will use [log probability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Log_probability) to automatically increase the temperature until certain thresholds are hit.

The parameters the functions accepts, described as a JSON Schema object. See the [guide](/docs/guides/function-calling) for examples, and the [JSON Schema reference](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/) for documentation about the format. 

Omitting `parameters` defines a function with an empty parameter list.

properties.name: strict
properties.description: Whether to enable strict schema adherence when generating the function call. If set to true, the model will follow the exact schema defined in the `parameters` field. Only a subset of JSON Schema is supported when `strict` is `true`. Learn more about Structured Outputs in the [function calling guide](docs/guides/function-calling).

properties.name: tool_resources
properties.description: A set of resources that are used by the assistant's tools. The resources are specific to the type of tool. For example, the `code_interpreter` tool requires a list of file IDs, while the `file_search` tool requires a list of vector store IDs.

properties.name: file_ids
properties.description: A list of [file](/docs/api-reference/files) IDs made available to the `code_interpreter`` tool. There can be a maximum of 20 files associated with the tool.

properties.name: vector_store_ids
properties.description: The ID of the [vector store](/docs/api-reference/vector-stores/object) attached to this assistant. There can be a maximum of 1 vector store attached to the assistant.

properties.name: metadata
properties.description:
Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to an object. This can be
useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured
format, and querying for objects via API or the dashboard. 

Keys are strings with a maximum length of 64 characters. Values are strings
with a maximum length of 512 characters.

properties.name: temperature
properties.description: What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.

properties.name: top_p
properties.description:
An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.

We generally recommend altering this or temperature but not both.

properties.name: response_format
properties.description: `auto` is the default value

properties.name: Text
properties.description: Default response format. Used to generate text responses.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of response format being defined. Always `text`.

properties.name: JSON object
properties.description:
JSON object response format. An older method of generating JSON responses.
Using `json_schema` is recommended for models that support it. Note that the
model will not generate JSON without a system or user message instructing it
to do so.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of response format being defined. Always `json_object`.

properties.name: JSON schema
properties.description:
JSON Schema response format. Used to generate structured JSON responses.
Learn more about [Structured Outputs](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of response format being defined. Always `json_schema`.

properties.name: json_schema
properties.description: Structured Outputs configuration options, including a JSON Schema.

properties.name: description
properties.description:
A description of what the response format is for, used by the model to
determine how to respond in the format.

properties.name: name
properties.description:
The name of the response format. Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain
underscores and dashes, with a maximum length of 64.

properties.name: schema
properties.description:
The schema for the response format, described as a JSON Schema object.
Learn how to build JSON schemas [here](https://json-schema.org/).

properties.name: strict
properties.description:
Whether to enable strict schema adherence when generating the output.
If set to true, the model will always follow the exact schema defined
in the `schema` field. Only a subset of JSON Schema is supported when
`strict` is `true`. To learn more, read the [Structured Outputs
guide](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

The entity to use for the run. This allows you to set the team or username of the WandB user that you would
like associated with the run. If not set, the default entity for the registered WandB API key is used.

properties.name: tags
properties.description:
A list of tags to be attached to the newly created run. These tags are passed through directly to WandB. Some
default tags are generated by OpenAI: "openai/finetune", "openai/{base-model}", "openai/{ftjob-abcdef}".

properties.name: seed
properties.description: The seed used for the fine-tuning job.

properties.name: estimated_finish
properties.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the fine-tuning job is estimated to finish. The value will be null if the fine-tuning job is not running.

properties.name: method
properties.description: The method used for fine-tuning.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of method. Is either `supervised` or `dpo`.

properties.name: supervised
properties.description: Configuration for the supervised fine-tuning method.

properties.name: hyperparameters
properties.description: The hyperparameters used for the fine-tuning job.

properties.name: dpo
properties.description: Configuration for the DPO fine-tuning method.

properties.name: hyperparameters
properties.description: The hyperparameters used for the fine-tuning job.

properties.name: metadata
properties.description:
Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to an object. This can be
useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured
format, and querying for objects via API or the dashboard. 

Keys are strings with a maximum length of 64 characters. Values are strings
with a maximum length of 512 characters.

properties.name: items
properties.description: Represents a step in execution of a run.

properties.name: id
properties.description: The identifier of the run step, which can be referenced in API endpoints.

properties.name: object
properties.description: The object type, which is always `thread.run.step`.

properties.name: created_at
properties.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run step was created.

properties.name: assistant_id
properties.description: The ID of the [assistant](/docs/api-reference/assistants) associated with the run step.

properties.name: thread_id
properties.description: The ID of the [thread](/docs/api-reference/threads) that was run.

properties.name: run_id
properties.description: The ID of the [run](/docs/api-reference/runs) that this run step is a part of.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of run step, which can be either `message_creation` or `tool_calls`.

properties.name: status
properties.description: The status of the run step, which can be either `in_progress`, `cancelled`, `failed`, `completed`, or `expired`.

properties.name: Message creation
properties.description: Details of the message creation by the run step.

properties.name: type
properties.description: Always `message_creation`.

properties.name: message_id
properties.description: The ID of the message that was created by this run step.

properties.name: Tool calls
properties.description: Details of the tool call.

properties.name: type
properties.description: Always `tool_calls`.

properties.name: tool_calls
properties.description: An array of tool calls the run step was involved in. These can be associated with one of three types of tools: `code_interpreter`, `file_search`, or `function`.

properties.name: Code Interpreter tool call
properties.description: Details of the Code Interpreter tool call the run step was involved in.

properties.name: id
properties.description: The ID of the tool call.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of tool call. This is always going to be `code_interpreter` for this type of tool call.

properties.name: code_interpreter
properties.description: The Code Interpreter tool call definition.

properties.name: input
properties.description: The input to the Code Interpreter tool call.

properties.name: outputs
properties.description: The outputs from the Code Interpreter tool call. Code Interpreter can output one or more items, including text (`logs`) or images (`image`). Each of these are represented by a different object type.

properties.name: Code Interpreter log output
properties.description: Text output from the Code Interpreter tool call as part of a run step.

properties.name: type
properties.description: Always `logs`.

properties.name: logs
properties.description: The text output from the Code Interpreter tool call.

properties.name: type
properties.description: Always `image`.

properties.name: file_id
properties.description: The [file](/docs/api-reference/files) ID of the image.

properties.name: id
properties.description: The ID of the tool call object.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of tool call. This is always going to be `file_search` for this type of tool call.

properties.name: file_search
properties.description: For now, this is always going to be an empty object.

properties.name: ranking_options
properties.description: The ranking options for the file search.

properties.name: ranker
properties.description: The ranker to use for the file search. If not specified will use the `auto` ranker.

properties.name: score_threshold
properties.description: The score threshold for the file search. All values must be a floating point number between 0 and 1.

properties.name: results
properties.description: The results of the file search.

properties.name: items
properties.description: A result instance of the file search.

properties.name: file_id
properties.description: The ID of the file that result was found in.

properties.name: file_name
properties.description: The name of the file that result was found in.

properties.name: score
properties.description: The score of the result. All values must be a floating point number between 0 and 1.

properties.name: content
properties.description: The content of the result that was found. The content is only included if requested via the include query parameter.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of the content.

properties.name: text
properties.description: The text content of the file.

properties.name: id
properties.description: The ID of the tool call object.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of tool call. This is always going to be `function` for this type of tool call.

properties.name: function
properties.description: The definition of the function that was called.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name of the function.

properties.name: arguments
properties.description: The arguments passed to the function.

properties.name: output
properties.description: The output of the function. This will be `null` if the outputs have not been [submitted](/docs/api-reference/runs/submitToolOutputs) yet.

properties.name: last_error
properties.description: The last error associated with this run step. Will be `null` if there are no errors.

properties.name: code
properties.description: One of `server_error` or `rate_limit_exceeded`.

properties.name: message
properties.description: A human-readable description of the error.

properties.name: expired_at
properties.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run step expired. A step is considered expired if the parent run is expired.

properties.name: cancelled_at
properties.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run step was cancelled.

properties.name: failed_at
properties.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run step failed.

properties.name: completed_at
properties.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run step completed.

properties.name: usage

properties.name: completion_tokens

properties.name: prompt_tokens

properties.description: The identifier, which can be referenced in API endpoints.

properties.name: object

properties.name: created_at
properties.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run was created.

properties.name: thread_id
properties.description: The ID of the [thread](/docs/api-reference/threads) that was executed on as a part of this run.

properties.name: assistant_id
properties.description: The ID of the [assistant](/docs/api-reference/assistants) used for execution of this run.

properties.description: Details on the tool outputs needed for this run to continue.

properties.name: tool_calls
properties.description: A list of the relevant tool calls.

properties.description: Tool call objects

properties.name: id
properties.description: The ID of the tool call. This ID must be referenced when you submit the tool outputs in using the [Submit tool outputs to run](/docs/api-reference/runs/submitToolOutputs) endpoint.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of tool call the output is required for. For now, this is always `function`.

properties.name: function
properties.description: The function definition.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name of the function.

properties.name: arguments
properties.description: The arguments that the model expects you to pass to the function.

properties.name: last_error
properties.description: The last error associated with this run. Will be `null` if there are no errors.

properties.name: code
properties.description: One of `server_error`, `rate_limit_exceeded`, or `invalid_prompt`.

properties.name: message
properties.description: A human-readable description of the error.

properties.name: expires_at
properties.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run will expire.

properties.name: started_at
properties.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run was started.

properties.name: cancelled_at
properties.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run was cancelled.

properties.name: failed_at
properties.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run failed.

properties.name: completed_at

properties.name: incomplete_details
properties.description: Details on why the run is incomplete. Will be `null` if the run is not incomplete.

properties.name: reason
properties.description: The reason why the run is incomplete. This will point to which specific token limit was reached over the course of the run.

properties.name: model
properties.description: The model that the [assistant](/docs/api-reference/assistants) used for this run.

properties.name: instructions
properties.description: The instructions that the [assistant](/docs/api-reference/assistants) used for this run.

properties.name: tools
properties.description: The list of tools that the [assistant](/docs/api-reference/assistants) used for this run.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of tool being defined: `code_interpreter`

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of tool being defined: `file_search`

properties.name: file_search
properties.description: Overrides for the file search tool.

properties.name: max_num_results
properties.description:
The maximum number of results the file search tool should output. The default is 20 for `gpt-4*` models and 5 for `gpt-3.5-turbo`. This number should be between 1 and 50 inclusive.

Note that the file search tool may output fewer than `max_num_results` results. See the [file search tool documentation](/docs/assistants/tools/file-search#customizing-file-search-settings) for more information.

properties.name: ranking_options
properties.description:
The ranking options for the file search. If not specified, the file search tool will use the `auto` ranker and a score_threshold of 0.

See the [file search tool documentation](/docs/assistants/tools/file-search#customizing-file-search-settings) for more information.

properties.name: ranker
properties.description: The ranker to use for the file search. If not specified will use the `auto` ranker.

properties.name: score_threshold
properties.description: The score threshold for the file search. All values must be a floating point number between 0 and 1.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of tool being defined: `function`

properties.name: description
properties.description: A description of what the function does, used by the model to choose when and how to call the function.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name of the function to be called. Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain underscores and dashes, with a maximum length of 64.

properties.name: parameters
properties.description:
The parameters the functions accepts, described as a JSON Schema object. See the [guide](/docs/guides/function-calling) for examples, and the [JSON Schema reference](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/) for documentation about the format. 

Omitting `parameters` defines a function with an empty parameter list.

properties.name: strict
properties.description: Whether to enable strict schema adherence when generating the function call. If set to true, the model will follow the exact schema defined in the `parameters` field. Only a subset of JSON Schema is supported when `strict` is `true`. Learn more about Structured Outputs in the [function calling guide](docs/guides/function-calling).

properties.name: metadata
properties.description:
Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to an object. This can be
useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured
format, and querying for objects via API or the dashboard. 

Keys are strings with a maximum length of 64 characters. Values are strings
with a maximum length of 512 characters.

properties.name: usage
properties.description: Usage statistics related to the run. This value will be `null` if the run is not in a terminal state (i.e. `in_progress`, `queued`, etc.).

properties.name: completion_tokens
properties.description: Number of completion tokens used over the course of the run.

properties.name: prompt_tokens
properties.description: Number of prompt tokens used over the course of the run.

properties.name: total_tokens
properties.description: Total number of tokens used (prompt + completion).

properties.name: temperature
properties.description: The sampling temperature used for this run. If not set, defaults to 1.

properties.name: top_p
properties.description: The nucleus sampling value used for this run. If not set, defaults to 1.

properties.name: max_prompt_tokens
properties.description: The maximum number of prompt tokens specified to have been used over the course of the run.

properties.name: max_completion_tokens
properties.description: The maximum number of completion tokens specified to have been used over the course of the run.

properties.name: parallel_tool_calls
properties.description: Whether to enable [parallel function calling](/docs/guides/function-calling#configuring-parallel-function-calling) during tool use.

properties.name: response_format
properties.description: `auto` is the default value

properties.name: Text
properties.description: Default response format. Used to generate text responses.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of response format being defined. Always `text`.

properties.name: JSON object
properties.description:
JSON object response format. An older method of generating JSON responses.
Using `json_schema` is recommended for models that support it. Note that the
model will not generate JSON without a system or user message instructing it
to do so.

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of response format being defined. Always `json_object`.

properties.name: JSON schema
properties.description:
JSON Schema response format. Used to generate structured JSON responses.
Learn more about [Structured Outputs](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

properties.name: type
properties.description: The type of response format being defined. Always `json_schema`.

properties.name: json_schema
properties.description: Structured Outputs configuration options, including a JSON Schema.

properties.name: description
properties.description:
A description of what the response format is for, used by the model to
determine how to respond in the format.

properties.name: name
properties.description:
The name of the response format. Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain
underscores and dashes, with a maximum length of 64.

properties.name: schema
properties.description:
The schema for the response format, described as a JSON Schema object.
Learn how to build JSON schemas [here](https://json-schema.org/).

properties.name: strict
properties.description:
Whether to enable strict schema adherence when generating the output.
If set to true, the model will always follow the exact schema defined
in the `schema` field. Only a subset of JSON Schema is supported when
`strict` is `true`. To learn more, read the [Structured Outputs
guide](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

properties.name: items
properties.description: A list of files attached to a vector store.

properties.name: id
properties.description: The identifier, which can be referenced in API endpoints.

properties.name: object
properties.description: The object type, which is always `vector_store.file`.

properties.name: usage_bytes
properties.description: The total vector store usage in bytes. Note that this may be different from the original file size.

properties.name: created_at
properties.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the vector store file was created.

properties.name: vector_store_id
properties.description: The ID of the [vector store](/docs/api-reference/vector-stores/object) that the [File](/docs/api-reference/files) is attached to.

properties.name: status
properties.description: The status of the vector store file, which can be either `in_progress`, `completed`, `cancelled`, or `failed`. The status `completed` indicates that the vector store file is ready for use.

properties.name: last_error
properties.description: The last error associated with this vector store file. Will be `null` if there are no errors.

properties.name: code
properties.description: One of `server_error` or `rate_limit_exceeded`.

properties.name: message
properties.description: A human-readable description of the error.

properties.name: type
properties.description: Always `static`.

properties.name: max_chunk_size_tokens
properties.description: The maximum number of tokens in each chunk. The default value is `800`. The minimum value is `100` and the maximum value is `4096`.

properties.name: chunk_overlap_tokens
properties.description:
The number of tokens that overlap between chunks. The default value is `400`.

Note that the overlap must not exceed half of `max_chunk_size_tokens`.

properties.name: Other Chunking Strategy
properties.description: This is returned when the chunking strategy is unknown. Typically, this is because the file was indexed before the `chunking_strategy` concept was introduced in the API.

properties.name: type
properties.description: Always `other`.

properties.name: temperature
properties.description:
What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.
We generally recommend altering this or `top_p` but not both.

properties.name: top_p
properties.description:
An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling,
where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability
mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass
are considered.

We generally recommend altering this or `temperature` but not both.

properties.name: user
properties.description: A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to monitor and detect abuse. [Learn more](/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#end-user-ids).

properties.name: service_tier
properties.description:
Specifies the latency tier to use for processing the request. This parameter is relevant for customers subscribed to the scale tier service:
  - If set to 'auto', and the Project is Scale tier enabled, the system
    will utilize scale tier credits until they are exhausted.
  - If set to 'auto', and the Project is not Scale tier enabled, the request will be processed using the default service tier with a lower uptime SLA and no latency guarentee.
  - If set to 'default', the request will be processed using the default service tier with a lower uptime SLA and no latency guarentee.
  - If set to 'flex', the request will be processed with the Flex Processing service tier. [Learn more](/docs/guides/flex-processing).
  - When not set, the default behavior is 'auto'.

  When this parameter is set, the response body will include the `service_tier` utilized.

properties.name: model
properties.description: ID of the model to use. You can use the [List models](/docs/api-reference/models/list) API to see all of your available models, or see our [Model overview](/docs/models) for descriptions of them.

properties.name: reasoning_effort
properties.description:
**o-series models only** 

Constrains effort on reasoning for 
[reasoning models](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/reasoning).
Currently supported values are `low`, `medium`, and `high`. Reducing
reasoning effort can result in faster responses and fewer tokens used
on reasoning in a response.

properties.name: max_num_results
properties.description:
The maximum number of results the file search tool should output. The default is 20 for `gpt-4*` models and 5 for `gpt-3.5-turbo`. This number should be between 1 and 50 inclusive.

Note that the file search tool may output fewer than `max_num_results` results. See the [file search tool documentation](/docs/assistants/tools/file-search#customizing-file-search-settings) for more information.

properties.name: ranking_options
properties.description:
The ranking options for the file search. If not specified, the file search tool will use the `auto` ranker and a score_threshold of 0.

See the [file search tool documentation](/docs/assistants/tools/file-search#customizing-file-search-settings) for more information.

properties.name: score_threshold
properties.description: The score threshold for the file search. All values must be a floating point number between 0 and 1.

properties.description: The name of the function to be called. Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain underscores and dashes, with a maximum length of 64.

properties.name: parameters
properties.description:
The parameters the functions accepts, described as a JSON Schema object. See the [guide](/docs/guides/function-calling) for examples, and the [JSON Schema reference](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/) for documentation about the format. 

Omitting `parameters` defines a function with an empty parameter list.

properties.name: strict
properties.description: Whether to enable strict schema adherence when generating the function call. If set to true, the model will follow the exact schema defined in the `parameters` field. Only a subset of JSON Schema is supported when `strict` is `true`. Learn more about Structured Outputs in the [function calling guide](docs/guides/function-calling).

properties.name: top_p

properties.name: response_format
properties.description:
Specifies the format that the model must output. Compatible with [GPT-4o](/docs/models#gpt-4o), [GPT-4 Turbo](/docs/models#gpt-4-turbo-and-gpt-4), and all GPT-3.5 Turbo models since `gpt-3.5-turbo-1106`.

Setting to `{ "type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {...} }` enables Structured Outputs which ensures the model will match your supplied JSON schema. Learn more in the [Structured Outputs guide](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

Setting to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables JSON mode, which ensures the message the model generates is valid JSON.

**Important:** when using JSON mode, you **must** also instruct the model to produce JSON yourself via a system or user message. Without this, the model may generate an unending stream of whitespace until the generation reaches the token limit, resulting in a long-running and seemingly "stuck" request. Also note that the message content may be partially cut off if `finish_reason="length"`, which indicates the generation exceeded `max_tokens` or the conversation exceeded the max context length.

properties.description: `auto` is the default value

Using `json_schema` is recommended for models that support it. Note that the
model will not generate JSON without a system or user message instructing it
to do so.

properties.name: type

properties.name: JSON schema

determine how to respond in the format.

underscores and dashes, with a maximum length of 64.

properties.name: schema
properties.description:
The schema for the response format, described as a JSON Schema object.
Learn how to build JSON schemas [here](https://json-schema.org/).

properties.name: strict

If set to true, the model will always follow the exact schema defined

guide](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).
